title: Invoices, bills, money owed to you and by you

sections.skill: Track invoices and bills as receivables and payables

questions.prompt: Money customers owe you is called what?
questions.correct_answer: Accounts receivable
questions.intro: An INVOICE is a bill YOU send to a customer; until it is paid, it is money owed TO you, called ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE. A BILL from a supplier is money YOU owe, called ACCOUNTS PAYABLE. A good invoice shows your business name, the customer, an invoice number, the date, what was provided, the amount, the due date and how to pay. Track both lists: who owes you, and whom you owe, with due dates. Paying bills on time protects your reputation with suppliers.

questions.prompt: A customer who has not paid your invoice holds an IOU to whom?
questions.correct_answer: To you
questions.intro: An IOU is a note that says "I owe you." In a business, IOUs go two ways. When you finish a job and send an invoice, the customer holds an IOU to you: that is a receivable. When a supplier sends you a bill, you hold an IOU to them: that is a payable. Keeping two lists, "owed to me" and "I owe," stops both kinds from being forgotten.
